result: AdaGrad gives every coordinate its own step size η/√(Σ g²) from the gradients seen so far, so rarely active features keep large steps. Its regret competes with the best diagonal preconditioner in hindsight, e.g. O(log d·√T) instead of O(√(dT)) for sparse data.
result_plain: Per-coordinate steps η/√(Σg²); regret adapts to the data, O(log d √T) on sparse features.
